example.theme: How to talk to a caveman

sessions.name: Before we start
sessions.summary: Guests are welcomed at the door, signed in and given a seat. Members catch up over coffee.

sessions.name: Opening
sessions.summary: The gavel comes down at 10:45 sharp. The President welcomes everyone and hands over to the host.

items.title: The host introduces the meeting and its theme

sessions.name: Prepared speeches
sessions.summary: Three members give speeches they've planned for weeks, each one a project on their learning path.

items.title: Speaker 1: an Ice Breaker, their very first speech

sessions.name: Table Topics
sessions.summary: Surprise questions, answered on the spot in one to two minutes. Volunteers only, guests welcome.

items.title: Vote for the best Table Topics speaker

sessions.name: Evaluations
sessions.summary: Every speaker hears what worked and one thing to try next time, from a member who listened closely.

sessions.name: Closing
sessions.summary: A look back at the whole meeting, then trophies, applause and a word from our guests.

items.title: Guest feedback and vote of thanks

roles.name: Toastmaster of the Day
roles.text: The host. Picks the theme, introduces every session and speaker, and keeps the morning flowing from one moment to the next.

roles.name: Speaker
roles.text: Delivers a prepared speech, five to seven minutes, that is one project on their Pathways learning path. A first speech, the Ice Breaker, runs four to six.

roles.name: Evaluator
roles.text: Listens to one speaker, then gives two to three minutes of kind, specific feedback: what worked, and one thing to try next time.

roles.name: Table Topics Master
roles.text: Prepares surprise questions on the theme and invites volunteers to answer them on the spot, in one to two minutes each.

roles.name: General Evaluator
roles.text: Evaluates the meeting itself: the evaluators, the roles, the timing and the energy in the room. Leads the evaluation team.

roles.name: Timer
roles.text: Times every speech and shows green, amber and red lights, so speakers know where they are without looking at a clock. Then reports the times.

roles.name: Grammarian
roles.text: Listens for the best phrases of the day, and for the ums and ahs. Reports both, kindly, near the end.

roles.name: Wordmaster
roles.text: Opens with a Word of the Day for everyone to try in their speeches, then reports who used it, and how well.

roles.name: Trivia Master
roles.text: Asks the room quick questions about what was said that morning. It keeps everyone listening, and it's fun.

roles.name: Elevator Pitch
roles.text: Two minutes on who you are and what you do. The best practice there is for networking, interviews and introductions.

roles.name: Sergeant at Arms
roles.text: Sets up the room, calls the meeting to order at 10:45, and makes sure everything is where it should be.

roles.name: President
roles.text: Welcomes everyone with a short address, and presents the awards at the close.

roles.name: Greet Master
roles.text: Meets guests at the door, signs them in and finds them a seat.

roles.name: Shoot Master
roles.text: Takes the photos, from the first speech to the group photo.

roles.name: Reel Master
roles.text: Films the moments that become the club's reels and stories.
